description: What: the matcher under load: k6 Kafka write rate and errors, arriving vs processed events, consumer lag (backlog), dead letters, matched vs zero-match, processing and trigger-matching time, active enrolments, DB pool, JVM and container. How: provisioned by monitoring/docker-compose.yml or imported into CCE's Grafana (monitoring/cce-grafana-import/README.md); pick the run in "Run id". Needs: DS_PROMETHEUS with k6 remote-write series (service="matcher"), the cce-matcher-service job and kafka-exporter (job kafka). Outputs: nothing written; panels and run annotations only.

panels.title: k6 → Kafka (topic cce.events.inbound), filtered by Run id and Test type

panels.description: Events k6 wrote to cce.events.inbound per second (xk6-kafka writer counters), and write errors. Any error fails the run (MATCHER_MAX_KAFKA_WRITE_ERRORS = 0). Verify both metric names at first scrape.
panels.title: k6 Kafka messages written / errors per second

panels.description: Iterations k6 should have started (open model) but could not, because all its virtual users were busy. A few are tolerated (MAX_DROPPED_RATE = 0.1 % of planned events, to be confirmed by the team). Many dropped iterations with LOW latency mean k6 itself is the limit ("at least X/s, k6 limit"), not the service; with HIGH latency the service is slow and k6 ran out of VUs waiting for it.
panels.title: k6 dropped iterations per minute

panels.description: Virtual users k6 has allocated to keep up with the arrival rate. In an open model this grows when responses get slower (each VU waits for its response). Reaching the scenario's maxVUs means the next iterations are dropped.
panels.title: k6 virtual users (each owns one Kafka producer)

panels.description: arriving = growth of the inbound topic (all producers: k6, and the collector during collector tests), from kafka-exporter; processed = events the matcher finished (cce_events_processed_total). While processed < arriving the backlog grows; after sending stops, processed shows the drain rate.
panels.title: Arriving vs processed per second

panels.description: Events in cce.events.inbound not yet read by the matcher's consumer group (kafka-exporter). The matcher does not export this itself, which is why the test tooling reads it with Kafka admin. Dashed line: MATCHER_MAX_BACKLOG = 1,000 (to be confirmed). After a flood: the time until 0 is the catch-up time; if it never reaches 0 the report says "not caught up".
panels.title: Backlog (consumer lag of cce-matcher-service)

panels.description: Total messages ever written to the dead-letter topic (events the matcher could not process). A rising line during a test is a failure (MATCHER_MAX_DEAD_LETTERS = 0 new records).
panels.title: Dead-letter topic size (cce.events.inbound.dlq)

panels.description: matched = the event triggered at least one ACTIVE plan definition (creates or advances enrolments); zero_match = no trigger matched. With a plan-definition set whose triggers fit the dataset, almost everything should be "matched"; many zero-matches point at wrong test data or inactive plan definitions.
panels.title: Matched vs zero-match per second

panels.description: Events the matcher had already processed (idempotency check on the CloudEvent id) and skipped. Should be 0 in a test with fresh ids.
panels.title: Duplicates skipped per second

panels.description: Errors while consuming from cce.events.inbound (deserialisation, processing exceptions). Should stay at 0.
panels.title: Inbound consumer errors per second

panels.description: End-to-end time the matcher spends on one event (timer cce.events.processing.duration): average over the last minute and the recent max. Rising average with a flat rate = the database or the number of ACTIVE plan definitions is slowing matching down.
panels.title: Processing time per event: average and max (ms)

panels.description: Part of the processing time spent matching the event against the triggers of the ACTIVE plan definitions (timer cce.step.matching.duration). Grows with the number of ACTIVE plan definitions an event matches and with their trigger rows (compare runs by plan_definition_set: emr-service vs kenya-sha-emr-service).
panels.title: Trigger matching time: average and max (ms)

panels.description: Time Spring Kafka spends in the matcher's listener per record (spring.kafka.listener timer). May be EMPTY: Spring only exports it when listener observation is on (verify at first scrape). Processing time above covers the same work.
panels.title: Kafka listener time (Spring): average and max (ms)

panels.description: Patients currently enrolled in a plan definition (gauge cce.protocol.instances.active). Grows with every new test patient that matches; a big number makes matching slower over time, which is why results record the data volume.
panels.title: Active protocol instances (enrolments)

panels.description: The service's database connection pool (HikariCP). active = connections running a query; idle = open but unused; pending = threads WAITING for a free connection; max = pool size. Pending above 0 means the database (or the pool size) is the bottleneck: requests queue for a connection before they can do any work.
panels.title: Hikari connections (matcher)

panels.description: Java heap memory in use. A saw-tooth is normal (garbage collection frees memory); a floor that keeps rising across a long run hints at a leak. The services run in 768 MiB containers locally. Service metrics carry no run id: use the time range and the run markers to find your run.
panels.title: JVM heap used

panels.description: Longest garbage-collection pause recently reported by the JVM. During a pause the service does no work, which shows up as latency spikes in k6. Pauses above 0.5 s are worth a note in the report.
panels.title: Longest GC pause

panels.description: CPU used by the cce-matcher-service container, in cores (1 = one full core), measured by cAdvisor from the container's cgroup. More reliable than the JVM's process_cpu_usage, which reports a share of the host. Empty if cAdvisor is not running or names containers differently.
panels.title: Container CPU (cores)

panels.description: Memory the cce-matcher-service container really uses (what the kernel would count against its limit), measured by cAdvisor.
panels.title: Container memory (working set)

list.description: Fixed on this dashboard: the k6 label "service" of this service's tests.
list.label: Service
list.name: service

list.description: k6 label "test_type": smoke, load, stress or breakpoint. Filters the k6 panels only.
list.label: Test type
list.name: test_type

list.description: Run id (k6 label "testid" = RUN_ID, e.g. 20261105-142233). Newest first. A Step SLA run has no k6 metrics: type its run id here (or add &var-testid=<runId> to the URL) to show its run markers.
list.label: Run id (testid)
list.name: testid
